CORRECTED. The ASV recasts the existential clause personally as 'he hath no pleasure', but no morpheme in the clause makes it possessive: there is no hāyâ, no possessive preposition (the bêt already holds its own 'in' before 'fools'), no suffix, and no verb the 'have' renders, since ʾên is rendered by 'no'. Rule 43's last case therefore leaves the supplied verb its own added unit together with the subject supplied alongside it, under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause, and forbids folding it into a preposition or noun standing elsewhere in the verse. Rule 50 keeps only a supplied dummy with the existential, and 'he' here is referential (God), not a dummy. The competing reading gives 'he hath no' whole to ʾên.

review_notes: Correction: 'he hath' was split off from the ʾên unit as its own added unit. Rule 43 places an English 'have' on whatever makes the clause possessive and, where nothing does, marks it added together with the subject supplied beside it; rule 50 keeps only a supplied dummy with the existential, and the 'he' of this clause is referential.
ʾên keeps the 'no' written for it and heads on the negation word (rule 50).
